children: Brazil's finance ministry extended a diesel fuel subsidy, effective on Sunday, citing persistent volatility in international oil and fuel prices, the ministry said in a statement on Saturday.
The subsidy began at 1.12 reais ($0.2159) per liter in late May, then rose to 2.12 reais per liter earlier this month as oil prices worsened
The original decree behind it expired on Friday, so the new decree takes over on Sunday to keep the full amount in place
Planning Minister Bruno Moretti had on Thursday signaled the extension was likely, pending a final decision from President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva

Moretti said that the oil price shock from the Middle East conflict has generated 50 billion reais ($9.64 billion) in extraordinary revenue against 40 billion reais in spending aimed at mitigating the conflict's impact
Government aims to remove the benefit once the oil price shock from the Middle East conflict dissipates
Brazil votes in the first round of its general election on October 4. Lula faces a close race with his leading right-wing rival, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro
